page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution at 2.8 GHz, accompanied by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It pairs these 48 vCPUs with 96 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute-optimized 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is focused strictly on CPU execution and cryptographic operations such as hardware-accelerated AES; there are no integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage drives included, requiring attached Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk storage.

The hardware configuration provides high sustained parallel execution and extensive I/O capacity, featuring a baseline network throughput of 150 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile performance across multi-core parallel workloads, including software compilation under Clang (score of 70,375.0) and Geekbench multi-core testing (23,747.0), while single-threaded tasks align with mid-tier industry averages. Memory subsystems yield top-tier uncached large-block read throughput of 402.56 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 198.42 GB/sec. This memory and network density translates into top-tier throughput for network I/O, achieving 101.03 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks and 101.5 million operations per second in Redis SET testing.

The qualitative tradeoff of the c8gn.12xlarge centers on its non-hyperthreaded ARM core architecture and external storage reliance. While single-thread throughput is unexceptional, the absence of simultaneous multithreading avoids thread contention, offering predictable multi-core execution efficiency. Combined with 150 Gbps network capacity, it is well tailored for large-scale distributed compilation pipelines, high-throughput network appliances, in-memory caches, and parallel compute-bound microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 48 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz, provisioned on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, it supplies 96 GB of system RAM without local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote EBS volumes. The architecture features a 150 Gbps baseline network interface and achieves top-tier multi-core compute marks, including 23,747.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 70,375.0 on Clang software compilation benchmarks. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 402.56 GB/sec, supporting top-tier static web serving throughput of 101.03 GB/sec and strong Redis operations at 101.5 million per second. While single-core performance remains average, the predictable execution of 48 dedicated physical cores and massive network bandwidth make it suited for parallel build pipelines, high-traffic web infrastructure, and distributed network processing.
